dedupe_keys.name: manage measured annual nutrient loads from agricultural environments database usda ars

description: A database of field-scale nitrogen and phosphorus export and site characteristics from published studies of US agricultural and forested land. The Ag Data Commons record says MANAGE began with 40 studies from an early 1980s compilation, gained 15 studies and runoff concentrations in 2008, added 30 forest runoff studies, 91 drainage water quality studies and 12 more runoff studies in 2016 with fertiliser timing, crop yield and nutrient uptake for 4R nutrient stewardship, and in 2022 added 27 studies and Level II ecoregion labels for each of 94 studies, covering 11 of the 50 North American Level II ecoregions. It was funded by USDA-ARS for the Conservation Effects Assessment Project and the Texas State Soil and Water Conservation Board. Two downloadable Microsoft Access databases are offered, version 6 of November 2021 (7.1 MB) and a zipped version 5 (0.8 MB), under CC0. Coverage is the major US agricultural regions under natural rainfall runoff and artificial drainage. Caveats: study sites are not a random sample, and the data are annual loads, not events. For simulation it gives measured nutrient loads by land use and practice, to calibrate runoff and water quality models used for drinking water intakes and drainage networks. A related catalogue record is the International Stormwater BMP Database.
